config_rule: configuration is read as libpwquality 1.4.4/1.4.5 reads it: /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf in strcmp order of names (a name whose first '.conf' ends it), then /etc/security/pwquality.conf (missing is allowed); '#' starts a comment anywhere; name and value are separated by whitespace and/or one '='; names are case-insensitive; the last assignment wins; an unknown setting, an invalid integer, a line longer than 1022 bytes or a NUL byte stops libpwquality reading and is ERROR here; a non-regular file is ERROR
dictionary_rule: when the module is enabled and dictcheck (module argument, else configuration, else default 1) is not 0, the cracklib dictionary files /var/cache/cracklib/cracklib_dict.pwd, .pwi and .hwm must be non-empty regular files; a missing or empty file is VALUE <cracklib-dictionary-missing> FAIL for every key, because pam_pwquality then rejects every new password; a non-regular file or an lstat error is ERROR; dictpath in the configuration or as a module argument is ERROR pwquality:dictpath-unsupported
error_value_contract: Every ERROR wire value is a stable <domain>:<reason> code.
module_rule: exactly one active line of type password (optionally '-password') in /etc/pam.d/common-password whose module basename is pam_pwquality.so and whose control is requisite or required; no such line is VALUE <module-absent> FAIL; more than one, a bracket control, a bracket argument, a line continuation or an @include line is ERROR
source_rule: fstec-configuration-2026 1.1 recommends password requisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3 minlen=15 ucredit=-1 lcredit=-1 dcredit=-1 ocredit=-1 for Debian/Ubuntu common-password or pwquality.conf; values by user decision 26.09.2026 (company policy): minlen at least 12, credits -1, retry 3
value_rule: VALUE is the effective integer: the last module argument key=value, else the configuration, else the default (minlen 8, credits 0, retry 1); minlen below 6 acts as 6 and retry below 1 as 1; a module argument of the key without a valid integer is ERROR
